category: AIP – Implementation and Integration
stem: A company manages a large-scale analytics platform that stores high-volume transaction data in a PostgreSQL database. The dataset includes hundreds of millions of records with customer details, purchase amounts, product categories, and regions. The analytics team wants to use Amazon SageMaker AI to predict which customers are likely to churn in the next 90 days and improve retention strategies. The company needs a solution that automates data extraction and preparation from the PostgreSQL database for scheduled cleaning, normalization, and handling of missing values. After refining the data, the team considers using SageMaker Feature Store to store and manage customer features for consistent inputs in machine learning workflows. Analysts should then be able to build and deploy a no-code churn-prediction model and easily generate predictions on new customer data without support from data scientists. Some architects also evaluated Amazon DocumentDB for the future modernization of application workloads. Which is the best option to achieve this requirement?

options.text: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate data from the PostgreSQL database into Amazon S3 continuously. Use AWS Glue DataBrew to clean and normalize the replicated dataset before importing it into SageMaker Canvas to build and deploy the churn-prediction model.
options.rationale: . While DMS is a powerful real-time data migration and synchronization service, it is primarily intended for scenarios requiring ongoing replication or minimal downtime migrations. In this case, the data extraction is periodic rather than continuous, so DMS would simply add unnecessary complexity and cost to the workflow. The scenario focuses on scheduled data preparation and no-code model building, not on maintaining a live replication pipeline.

options.text: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to extract and clean the dataset from PostgreSQL. Apply AWS Glue Data Quality to define and validate data quality rules, then attempt to build the churn-prediction model directly within DataBrew.
options.rationale: . AWS Glue DataBrew is primarily designed for visual data preparation, while AWS Glue Data Quality focuses on defining and validating data quality rules. Neither service supports training, deploying, or generating predictions from machine learning models. The requirement clearly states that analysts must build and deploy a no-code churn-prediction model, which DataBrew and Data Quality cannot provide. Therefore, this option only addresses data preparation and validation but fails to deliver the no-code ML modeling and prediction capabilities required in the scenario.

options.text: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to extract the data from PostgreSQL, clean and normalize the dataset, and write the prepared data back into Amazon S3. Import the cleaned dataset into SageMaker Canvas to build a no-code churn-prediction model and generate predictions for business analysts.

Use AWS Glue DataBrew to prepare and clean the data from the PostgreSQL database. Use SageMaker Studio to build, train, and deploy a custom churn-prediction model using a notebook-based workflow for data scientists.
options.rationale: . SageMaker Studio is typically designed for data scientists who build models using code and notebook-based workflows. The requirement clearly specifies a no-code solution that allows business analysts to create and generate churn predictions independently. Since Studio requires technical expertise and coding, it does not meet the no-code requirement of the scenario.

correct_text: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to extract the data from PostgreSQL, clean and normalize the dataset, and write the prepared data back into Amazon S3. Import the cleaned dataset into SageMaker Canvas to build a no-code churn-prediction model and generate predictions for business analysts.
razon_rescate: Ninguna carta ensena SageMaker Canvas (modelado no-code) ni DataBrew para prep->Canvas; las cartas tratan migracion de bases de datos y dedup, solape solo de escenario (PostgreSQL/Glue).

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A healthcare organization is building an enterprise search tool using Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. The underlying corporate data resides in an Amazon S3 data lake, which is cataloged using AWS Glue. The organization must enforce strict access controls to ensure that different departments can only query documents that correspond to specific departmental data. The security team wants to implement fine-grained access control at the database, table, and column level using a scalable, attribute-based approach rather than managing complex AWS IAM policies for every individual user and resource combination. Which solution will securely meet these requirements with the least operational overhead?

options.text: Implement AWS Lake Formation and assign an LF-Tag to the databases, tables, and columns representing the departmental data. Grant IAM principals access to the data lake resources based on the matching LF-Tag expressions.

Use Amazon Macie to discover sensitive data within the S3 buckets. Trigger an AWS Lambda function to move the sensitive documents into separate, department-specific S3 buckets with strict bucket policies.
options.rationale: because Amazon Macie is a data security service that discovers sensitive data; it is not an access control management system for data catalogs and does not support column-level filtering.

options.text: Utilize AWS CloudFormation Guard to enforce policy-as-code rules on the Glue Data Catalog. Ensure that the queries generated by Bedrock are validated against the authorized schema before execution.
options.rationale: because CloudFormation Guard is just an open-source evaluation tool for validating infrastructure-as-code templates against compliance rules, not a runtime query interception or data access control tool.

options.text: Configure IAM identity-based policies with resource tags. Attach these policies to the roles assumed by the Bedrock Knowledge Bases to restrict access to specific S3 buckets based on department tags.
options.rationale: because AWS IAM policies and standard resource tags primarily control access at the bucket or object level, failing to provide the column-level and table-level fine-grained access required by the security team.

correct_text: Implement AWS Lake Formation and assign an LF-Tag to the databases, tables, and columns representing the departmental data. Grant IAM principals access to the data lake resources based on the matching LF-Tag expressions.
razon_rescate: El servicio/feature EXACTO (Lake Formation LF-Tags, permisos por tag expression) no se ensena; las cartas tratan SCP/Organizations, otro mecanismo de acceso. | La AIP exige LF-Tags a nivel columna (feature especifica no ensenada); las cartas solo definen SCP a nivel de cuenta, menor profundidad y ot

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A company has developed a machine learning-based recommendation system designed to personalize content for users. The model has been trained using Amazon SageMaker AI built-in algorithms and a custom dataset, with real-time inference being performed within SageMaker AI. As part of the system, the company also intends to leverage Amazon Comprehend for natural language processing to analyze customer reviews and sentiment, which will further enhance the recommendation engine. To meet strict security and compliance requirements, the company must ensure that both the training and inference environments, as well as all associated services, are deployed within a secure Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). Furthermore, the solution must completely block all access to the internet or any external resources to protect sensitive user data and ensure compliance with regulatory standards. Which of the following will satisfy the given requirements with the LEAST development effort?

options.text: Set up SageMaker AI within a VPC only mode and establish a VPC peering connection to enable Comprehend access in a different VPC.
options.rationale: because VPC peering introduces additional complexity in routing, security group configuration, and maintenance. It typically requires careful setup to ensure no unintended internet access is allowed, which increases development effort and risk.

options.text: Deploy SageMaker AI in VPC only mode and configure an internet gateway with restrictive security group rules to block external access.
options.rationale: because the presence of an internet gateway contradicts the requirement to completely block internet access. Security group rules alone cannot guarantee full isolation, and the existence of an internet gateway introduces the possibility of misconfiguration or accidental exposure, which would fail compliance audits.

options.text: Activate SageMaker AI network isolation mode to block all external access and establish a VPC endpoint for Comprehend within the same VPC.
Use VPC only mode for SageMaker AI, configure a network access control list (NACL) to block internet access, and allow traffic to Comprehend.
options.rationale: because NACLs (Network Access Control Lists) are not sufficient to fully block all external access and provide the same level of security as SageMaker’s network isolation mode. While NACLs can primarily restrict internet access, they do not provide complete isolation from external resources, as traffic could still flow via routes other than the NACLs. Moreover, this option does not use VPC endpoints to securely connect to Amazon Comprehend, leaving room for potential security risks.

correct_text: Activate SageMaker AI network isolation mode to block all external access and establish a VPC endpoint for Comprehend within the same VPC.
razon_rescate: Ninguna carta ensena network isolation mode combinado con VPC endpoint para Comprehend; el solape es solo tematico (VPC/privacidad).

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A large retail company is looking to leverage Amazon SageMaker AI notebooks and Amazon Comprehend to process and analyze customer feedback data. The company uses Amazon S3 buckets to store large datasets of customer reviews, and the data needs to be accessed securely for machine learning analysis. Given the sensitivity of the data, the company mandates that all resources must remain within a secure Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). Additionally, all communication must occur over the AWS network. Which solution will satisfy the given requirements?

options.text: Deploy the SageMaker AI notebook in a private subnet with a route to an internet gateway and ensure that all data requests to S3 are routed through an external proxy.
options.rationale: because routing through an internet gateway and external proxy exposes traffic to the public internet, violating the requirement that all communication must occur over a private AWS network.

options.text: Deploy the SageMaker AI notebook in a private subnet within a VPC and use a VPC Peering connection with another VPC where S3 is accessible.
options.rationale: because VPC peering does not typically provide private access to AWS services like S3. Accessing S3 through a peered VPC still requires public endpoints unless VPC endpoints are configured, which this option does not guarantee.

options.text: Deploy the SageMaker AI notebook in a private subnet within a VPC and ensure that the VPC has private endpoints for both SageMaker AI and S3.
Deploy the SageMaker AI notebook in a private subnet, use a NAT gateway to provide outbound internet access for S3, and restrict access to only specific S3 buckets.
options.rationale: because using a NAT gateway primarily involves public internet routing, which contradicts the mandate for a private AWS network. Even with bucket restrictions, the traffic path does not meet the security requirements.

correct_text: Deploy the SageMaker AI notebook in a private subnet within a VPC and ensure that the VPC has private endpoints for both SageMaker AI and S3.
razon_rescate: Las cartas identifican el servicio Comprehend, no ensenan el despliegue con VPC endpoints privados para notebook+S3; solape solo de escenario.

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A data science team is leveraging Amazon SageMaker AI to build and deploy machine learning models for predictive analytics. The team also uses Amazon Comprehend to perform natural language processing (NLP) on text data as part of an analysis pipeline. The SageMaker notebook instances are deployed within an isolated Amazon VPC to ensure that the development work is secure. VPC interface endpoints were set up to establish private connectivity between the VPC and the SageMaker API. The team is also exploring the AWS Strands API as part of broader AI tooling initiatives. The team later discovers that unauthorized users from outside the VPC can still access the notebook instances through the internet, raising security concerns. How can the team limit access to the SageMaker notebook instances, ensuring only authorized VPC users can connect?

options.text: Update the security group for the notebook instances to restrict incoming traffic to only the CIDR blocks associated with the VPC. Apply this security group across all interfaces linked to the SageMaker notebook instances.
options.rationale: because configuring a security group only restricts traffic at the network interface level. While this approach controls access to the instances themselves, it does not prevent users from accessing the SageMaker API over the internet, which is required to interact with the notebook instances. Therefore, this method does not fully secure access to the notebook instances.

options.text: Configure an IAM policy that allows sagemaker:CreatePresignedNotebookInstanceUrl and sagemaker:DescribeNotebookInstance actions exclusively from VPC interface endpoints. Ensure this policy is applied to the appropriate IAM users, groups, and roles.
Set up VPC Traffic Mirroring to capture traffic to and from the notebook instances and identify unauthorized access attempts, enabling enhanced monitoring.
options.rationale: because VPC Traffic Mirroring is a monitoring tool that primarily captures and inspects network traffic. It does not block or restrict access to resources. While it helps in identifying unauthorized access attempts, it does not prevent them from occurring, making it unsuitable for securing the notebook instances themselves.

options.text: Apply VPC Endpoint Policies to control which IAM users or services can access SageMaker AI through the VPC interface endpoint, providing more granular access control for interactions with SageMaker AI.
options.rationale: because VPC Endpoint Policies typically control access to AWS services over the VPC endpoint but do not restrict access to the SageMaker notebook instances themselves. They manage which users or services can access the SageMaker API through the endpoint, but they do not secure the notebook instances from unauthorized access.

correct_text: Configure an IAM policy that allows sagemaker:CreatePresignedNotebookInstanceUrl and sagemaker:DescribeNotebookInstance actions exclusively from VPC interface endpoints. Ensure this policy is applied to the appropriate IAM users, groups, and roles.
razon_rescate: El objetivo exacto (condicion IAM sobre acciones sagemaker: restringidas a VPC endpoint) no aparece en ninguna carta; solo solape de tema VPC. | La AIP pide una decision de diseno IAM a nivel de accion/condicion; las cartas solo definen aislamiento de red. Bloom AIP=alto vs carta=medio.
feature_faltante: IAM policy condicionada a VPC endpoint sobre acciones sagemaker:*; strands

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: A Generative AI engineering team is developing a supervised image recognition model to accurately identify pandas from a diverse dataset of wildlife photographs. Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth is used to label 1,000 panda images and split the data into training and testing sets, reserving 100 images as a constant test set. Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels is then configured to train a custom image classification model capable of recognizing distinctive panda features such as fur patterns, posture, and environmental background. During the evaluation phase, the engineering team observes that the image classifier misclassifies several test images. A closer analysis reveals that in more than 75% of the misclassified images, the pandas appear upside down, indicating the model’s sensitivity to image orientation. The team must enhance the model’s ability to correctly identify pandas regardless of orientation, without collecting an entirely new dataset or extensively modifying the existing training pipeline. Which approach will most effectively enhance the model’s accuracy in addressing this specific misclassification issue?

options.text: Implement normalization preprocessing steps to make all images share a common scale and brightness distribution.
options.rationale: because normalization primarily standardizes image pixel intensity and brightness levels to ensure consistent numerical input during model training. While this process improves training stability and gradient performance, it does not enhance a model’s ability to recognize objects from different orientations or poses, which is the main issue described in the scenario.

options.text: Raise the number of training epochs to prolong optimization and reinforce feature representation within the existing dataset.
options.rationale: because increasing the number of epochs simply causes the model to iterate over the same dataset multiple times. This can reduce training loss but does not address the lack of visual diversity in the images. Without new data variations, the model remains sensitive to image orientation and may even overfit to existing patterns instead of learning rotational invariance.

options.text: Expand the existing training dataset by introducing data augmentation techniques such as image rotation, flipping, and scaling.
Apply transfer learning techniques to reuse a proven vision model’s base layers while retraining task-specific layers for panda identification.
options.rationale: because transfer learning typically accelerates model training and leverages existing learned features, but cannot overcome orientation-specific bias when the dataset lacks diversity. It improves feature extraction for similar visual patterns but does not replace the need for augmentation methods that expose the model to multiple orientations during training.

correct_text: Expand the existing training dataset by introducing data augmentation techniques such as image rotation, flipping, and scaling.
razon_rescate: Ninguna carta ensena data augmentation; ensenan seleccion de algoritmos de vision, objetivo distinto.

category: AIP – Testing, Validation, and Troubleshooting
stem: An AI developer is tasked with building a generative AI system to summarize patient medical records for physicians. The system uses Amazon SageMaker AI to fine-tune a large language model (LLM) on sensitive clinical notes stored in Amazon S3. Amazon Comprehend Medical is used to extract key medical entities from clinical notes, enriching the dataset for training. After generating summaries, the developer must ensure outputs are clinically relevant, accurate, and compliant with regulatory standards. Due to the high stakes of medical decision-making, a robust process is required to enable healthcare professionals to review and correct AI-generated summaries before full deployment. The solution must scale to handle large volumes of records and integrate seamlessly with existing SageMaker pipelines for smooth retraining and deployment. Which approach will best satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Use SageMaker Model Monitor to detect and flag low-confidence summaries for physician review, and store flagged cases in S3 for manual review before full deployment.
options.rationale: . Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor is primarily designed to detect data drift, bias, or quality issues in deployed models, rather than establishing a structured human review workflow. While it can flag low-confidence predictions, it does not provide a built-in mechanism for human validation or correction of outputs. It would only serve as a monitoring layer, rather than enabling continuous feedback integration from medical professionals.

options.text: Leverage Amazon Bedrock's knowledge base to enhance the model's training dataset with additional external knowledge. Improve the model's performance before deployment.
options.rationale: . Amazon Bedrock’s knowledge base is primarily used to enrich large language models with external data sources for better accuracy and retrieval-augmented generation. However, it would just help expand the model’s knowledge and not ensure the clinical correctness or compliance of generated summaries. In healthcare, regulatory validation requires explicit human review, something this option simply cannot guarantee.

options.text: Implement Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) to create a human review process. Allow healthcare professionals to validate and refine AI-generated summaries before deployment at scale.
options.rationale: . Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) is typically used for specific human review tasks during inference, such as document classification or moderation, rather than full-scale data labeling and retraining workflows. Ground Truth Plus extends this functionality by offering managed human review and scalable labeling operations ideal for regulated industries.

options.text: Use SageMaker Ground Truth Plus to create a human-in-the-loop workflow for expert validation and correction of model-generated summaries. Integrate this workflow with the existing SageMaker pipeline for seamless model retraining and deployment.

correct_text: Use SageMaker Ground Truth Plus to create a human-in-the-loop workflow for expert validation and correction of model-generated summaries. Integrate this workflow with the existing SageMaker pipeline for seamless model retraining and deployment.
razon_rescate: El servicio/feature EXACTO (Ground Truth Plus, HITL de revision) no se ensena en ninguna carta. | La AIP evalua una feature especifica (Ground Truth Plus HITL) y su integracion; las cartas solo definen servicios NLP. Bloom AIP=alto vs carta=medio.
feature_faltante: SageMaker Ground Truth Plus; human-in-the-loop; fine-tune

category: AIP – Implementation and Integration
stem: A data science team at a retail company wants to predict customer churn based on various historical transactional data. The dataset contains 10,000 records, each with 1,500 attributes, such as demographic information, purchasing patterns, and customer service interactions. The team is looking for an automated way to build a model using Amazon SageMaker AI, which can predict whether a customer will churn while also identifying the most relevant features contributing to the prediction. To deepen insights, the team uses Amazon Comprehend to analyze sentiment and key phrases in customer interactions. Which of the following solutions will best fulfill these requirements while minimizing manual effort?

options.text: Use SageMaker Ground Truth to label customer churn data, then build a custom TensorFlow model to predict churn and analyze feature weights post-training.
options.rationale: because it requires manual data labeling and building a custom TensorFlow model for churn prediction adds more manual intervention, as the team would need to fine-tune the model, analyze feature weights post-training, and handle the full model development process, making it less automated compared to SageMaker Autopilot.

options.text: Use the k-means algorithm in SageMaker AI to cluster customers based on purchasing patterns. After clustering, use the resulting clusters to predict churn based on customer behavior.
options.rationale: because k-means is an unsupervised learning algorithm typically used for clustering, not classification. It doesn’t directly predict churn, and using clusters for prediction would require additional modeling steps and assumptions.

options.text: Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to automatically train a churn prediction model and rely on its quick model visualization feature to generate accurate importance scores for deployment decisions.
options.rationale: because Data Wrangler is primarily designed for data preparation and visualization, not for automated model training or deep feature attribution. It lacks the end-to-end automation and interpretability features provided by Autopilot and Clarify.

options.text: Leverage SageMaker Autopilot to automatically train a classification model for forecasting customer churn. Then, utilize insights from SageMaker Clarify to determine which features most significantly influence the predictions.

correct_text: Leverage SageMaker Autopilot to automatically train a classification model for forecasting customer churn. Then, utilize insights from SageMaker Clarify to determine which features most significantly influence the predictions.
razon_rescate: Ninguna carta ensena la combinacion Autopilot+Clarify para importancia de features; solape solo de escenario (churn/SageMaker).

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A developer is working on an advanced machine learning project using Amazon SageMaker AI. The project involves training a deep learning model using large datasets stored in Amazon S3. Additionally, the developer needs to store model artifacts, logs, and evaluation results back to a different S3 bucket upon completion of the training job. To ensure security and proper access control, the developer must grant the SageMaker notebook instance appropriate permissions to read from and write to the specific S3 buckets. Which approach should be used to securely enable this access?

options.text: Define a bucket policy on the S3 bucket that allows the SageMaker AI notebook instance by its ARN to perform s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, and s3:ListBucket actions.
options.rationale: because while bucket policies can typically grant access, they are better suited for cross-account access or broader permissions. Managing access through IAM roles is more maintainable, secure, and aligned with AWS best practices for service-to-service communication.

options.text: Create an S3 access point for the SageMaker notebook instance, granting it access to the necessary data, and configure the access point to allow only the required actions (s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, and s3:ListBucket).
options.rationale: because S3 Access Points are primarily designed for managing access to shared datasets at scale, especially in multi-tenant environments. For a single SageMaker notebook instance, using an IAM role is simpler, more direct, and avoids unnecessary complexity.

options.text: Allow the SageMaker notebook instance to perform s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, and s3:ListBucket operations by attaching a policy to its associated IAM role that grants access to the designated S3 buckets.
Use AWS IAM identity federation to provide temporary access to the S3 bucket by configuring the SageMaker notebook instance to assume a federated role for accessing the data.
options.rationale: because IAM identity federation is intended for external identities (e.g., corporate users or third-party apps), not for AWS services like SageMaker AI. SageMaker AI should use its IAM role for access, not federated identities.

correct_text: Allow the SageMaker notebook instance to perform s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, and s3:ListBucket operations by attaching a policy to its associated IAM role that grants access to the designated S3 buckets.
razon_rescate: Ninguna carta ensena como respuesta correcta otorgar s3:GetObject/PutObject/ListBucket al role del notebook; los permisos S3 solo aparecen como distractor de una carta de KMS, y falta PutObject (escritura).

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A financial services company is developing a machine learning (ML) model in Amazon SageMaker AI to detect real-time fraudulent transactions. The company plans to integrate this model with Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for continuous transaction data ingestion and Amazon DynamoDB for storing transaction metadata. The model must be trained on an extensive historical dataset stored in Amazon S3. The company must ensure that all data is encrypted in transit and at rest, and that access to sensitive data and model results is strictly controlled. AWS Encryption SDK is being considered for additional client-side encryption of sensitive data before uploading it to S3. There’s also a need to track model performance over time to ensure it remains effective and predictions align with business rules. Which solution will secure the ML workflow, control access, and allow for continuous monitoring of model performance?

options.text: Use SageMaker AI to train the model with data from S3, enable S3 server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) for data at rest, configure IAM roles to control access to the model and data, and use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor model performance metrics and logging.

Use SageMaker AI to train the model with data from S3, enable S3 server-side encryption (SSE-S3) for data at rest, store model results in S3 with IAM roles to control access, and use Amazon Macie for monitoring sensitive data exposure.
options.rationale: . While SSE-S3 provides encryption for data at rest, it does not offer the same level of fine-grained access control and auditability as SSE-KMS. SSE-KMS allows for customer-managed encryption keys, which are crucial for compliance requirements in industries like financial services, where audit trails and access control are necessary. Additionally, Amazon Macie is a service primarily designed to identify and protect sensitive data within Amazon S3, such as PII (Personally Identifiable Information), but it does not monitor model performance or control access to the model itself. Therefore, Amazon Macie is not the right tool for ensuring the security and performance monitoring of the model in this scenario.

options.text: Utilize SageMaker AI to train the model with data from S3, store the model and metadata in DynamoDB, and configure Amazon VPC endpoints for secure communication between the SageMaker AI instance, DynamoDB, and Kinesis Data Streams. Use AWS CloudTrail to monitor access and activity.
options.rationale: because DynamoDB is not optimized for storing large ML models. DynamoDB is more suitable for fast access to small pieces of data, like metadata, rather than large model artifacts. Storing the model in S3 is more appropriate as it is designed for scalable storage of large objects, including model files. Additionally, CloudTrail is typically used to monitor API activity, not to monitor model performance, which is a critical aspect of maintaining an effective ML model. In this scenario, Amazon CloudWatch is the appropriate service for monitoring the model’s performance metrics and ensuring it continues to meet business requirements.

options.text: Use SageMaker AI to train the model with data from S3, configure Amazon Data Firehose to ingest the transaction data into SageMaker AI, and use AWS Glue to catalog the transaction data. Use Amazon CloudWatch for model performance monitoring and IAM policies to restrict access.
options.rationale: because Amazon Data Firehose is just used for streaming data into services like Amazon S3 or Amazon Redshift, but it is not necessary for real-time fraud detection or training the model in Amazon SageMaker AI. The model can ingest data directly from Kinesis Data Streams or S3 without the need for Data Firehose. Additionally, AWS Glue is primarily a service for data cataloging and ETL (Extract, Transform, Load), which is not required for the real-time transaction data ingestion in this fraud detection scenario. The focus should be on SageMaker AI’s ability to directly integrate with data sources like S3 and Kinesis for training and inference.

correct_text: Use SageMaker AI to train the model with data from S3, enable S3 server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) for data at rest, configure IAM roles to control access to the model and data, and use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor model performance metrics and logging.
razon_rescate: Ninguna carta ensena la combinacion de seguridad+monitoreo del flujo ML (SSE-KMS+IAM+CloudWatch para SageMaker); solape solo de tema seguridad/fraude.

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: An AI developer is building a fraud detection model using Amazon SageMaker Autopilot to generate and evaluate candidate models automatically. To further refine model performance, the developer integrates automatic model tuning (AMT) in Amazon SageMaker AI to optimize several hyperparameters related to model learning rate, batch size, and regularization strength. The team also applies canary testing to validate top-performing candidate models before full deployment. During multiple tuning jobs, the developer notices that some training jobs run unnecessarily long when the model’s validation accuracy stops improving early in the process. The tuning configuration must be adjusted appropriately to optimize resource usage and reduce overall tuning time, allowing SageMaker AI to decide automatically when to stop poorly performing training jobs. Which configuration step should be taken to address this requirement?

options.text: Modify the objective metric in the tuning job definition to use a stricter validation threshold, ensuring underperforming models are ignored automatically.
options.rationale: . Changing the objective metric or its threshold does not automatically stop unproductive training jobs. It only affects how SageMaker AI ranks models after training is complete, not how long each training job runs. The issue in the scenario concerns resource optimization during training, not post-training model selection. Therefore, modifying the metric threshold would not address unnecessary compute usage during tuning.

options.text: Increase the MaxRuntimeInSeconds parameter in the tuning job configuration to allow more time for underperforming training jobs to complete.
options.rationale: . Increasing the maximum runtime would simply extend how long each training job can run, which is the opposite of the developer’s desire. The goal is to reduce wasted compute time, not increase it. The MaxRuntimeInSeconds parameter is typically used to enforce an upper limit on runtime for training jobs that need strict time control, not to manage early stopping or performance improvement detection.

options.text: Enable early stopping by setting the TrainingJobEarlyStoppingType parameter to the AUTO value in the tuning job configuration.
Configure the tuning strategy to use Bayesian optimization, ensuring that all training jobs complete fully before evaluating results.
options.rationale: . Bayesian optimization primarily controls how new hyperparameter combinations are selected based on previous results. It does not influence how long each training job runs or whether jobs stop early. In fact, forcing all jobs to complete fully would only waste additional resources when no further improvement is expected. Early stopping is a separate configuration designed precisely to avoid this inefficiency.

correct_text: Enable early stopping by setting the TrainingJobEarlyStoppingType parameter to the AUTO value in the tuning job configuration.
razon_rescate: El parametro/feature exacto (TrainingJobEarlyStoppingType=AUTO, early stopping en AMT) no se ensena; las cartas definen AMT en general. | La AIP pide un parametro/valor concreto de configuracion; las cartas solo definen que existe AMT. Bloom AIP=alto vs carta=medio.

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: A retail analytics company is training a recommendation model using Amazon SageMaker AI, with training data stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The team uses SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning (AMT) to optimize hyperparameters such as learning rate and maximum depth, and tracks the best-performing models in the SageMaker Model Registry. During tuning, many jobs continue running even after early validation results indicate poor performance, resulting in unnecessary GPU usage. The company wants a tuning strategy that automatically stops underperforming trials and reallocates resources to promising configurations to reduce compute costs. Which tuning strategy should be employed to enhance optimization efficiency and expedite hyperparameter search?

options.text: Implement Bayesian optimization to refine the hyperparameter search space iteratively.
options.rationale: . Bayesian optimization is a powerful tuning strategy that efficiently explores the hyperparameter space by building a probabilistic model of performance. However, it does not automatically terminate underperforming trials early. It focuses primarily on selecting the following promising configuration based on prior results rather than dynamically reallocating compute resources. In this scenario, where cost efficiency and early stopping are crucial, Bayesian optimization alone would not prevent unnecessary GPU usage.

options.text: Utilize the Hyperband strategy in SageMaker AI to allocate resources efficiently and early stop weak trials.
Use grid search to evaluate all possible hyperparameter combinations without early stopping exhaustively.
options.rationale: . Grid search simply tests every combination of hyperparameters in a predefined range, which makes it highly inefficient for large search spaces. It typically consumes excessive computational resources and time because every job runs to completion regardless of performance. This brute-force method is useful for small experiments but does not support early stopping or adaptive resource allocation, making it unsuitable for efficiently optimizing complex models.

options.text: Utilize random search to sample hyperparameter combinations uniformly across the search space.
options.rationale: . While it can sometimes find good configurations faster than grid search, it still lacks any built-in mechanism to stop poorly performing jobs early. It simply runs each trial to completion, which typically wastes resources on weak configurations. Random search does not provide the intelligent resource management and adaptive early stopping offered by Hyperband, making it less cost-effective for large-scale tuning tasks.

correct_text: Utilize the Hyperband strategy in SageMaker AI to allocate resources efficiently and early stop weak trials.
razon_rescate: La estrategia especifica Hyperband no se ensena; las cartas solo mencionan AMT/HPO como concepto. | La AIP distingue una sub-feature (estrategia Hyperband) frente a otras estrategias; las cartas solo definen AMT como concepto. Bloom AIP=alto vs carta=medio.

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: A research division is continuously retraining a Generative Forecasting Foundation model pipeline built on Amazon SageMaker AI, where base embedding creation happens in SageMaker Processing, feature encoding is performed inside the SageMaker Feature Store ingestion pipeline, and final supervised regression is trained in SageMaker Training. Last quarter, this same regression model was tuned using SageMaker AI automatic model tuning (AMT), and the results produced a known stable set of high-performing hyperparameters that were saved. A new quarter dataset is now being ingested, and it is larger, has a different distribution, and must be used for the next model update. However, the engineering pillar requires that a new hyperparameter tuning job cannot start from zero because the compute budget is limited. There is also a requirement that if the model’s validation loss does not improve anymore, the tuning must automatically stop without manual intervention. Which hyperparameter tuning job configuration should be used?

options.text: Configure a warm start hyperparameter tuning job with the IDENTICAL_DATA_AND_ALGORITHM warm start mode and enable AMT Early Stopping to automatically terminate exploration as soon as validation loss stops improving.
options.rationale: because IDENTICAL_DATA_AND_ALGORITHM primarily assumes the same dataset and algorithm. Since the new dataset has a different distribution and size, this mode is invalid and could lead to suboptimal tuning or errors.

options.text: Start a warm start hyperparameter tuning job using the TRANSFER_LEARNING warm start type to import the previously saved tuning job results. Enable AMT Early Stopping to automatically terminate exploration as soon as validation loss stops improving when training with the new quarterly dataset.

Execute a hyperparameter tuning job with a newly expanded search space using the same algorithm container. Rely on Bayesian Optimization inside SageMaker AI AMT to naturally rediscover higher-performing parameter combinations using the new quarterly dataset, which will naturally guide convergence efficiency without importing prior tuning job results.
options.rationale: because it ignores the compute budget constraint. Starting from scratch with Bayesian Optimization may be effective, but it’s inefficient when prior tuning results are available and reuse is explicitly required.

options.text: Run a new hyperparameter tuning job using SageMaker AMT Hyperband strategy, allowing the system to aggressively eliminate poorly performing training jobs early while exploring the new quarterly dataset with wider search ranges. Depend on Hyperband efficiency itself rather than importing prior warm start knowledge from the previously tuned model.
options.rationale: because while Hyperband typically improves efficiency through early termination of poor-performing trials, it still starts tuning from scratch and does not leverage any past tuning job results. This leads to unnecessary compute expenditure.

correct_text: Start a warm start hyperparameter tuning job using the TRANSFER_LEARNING warm start type to import the previously saved tuning job results. Enable AMT Early Stopping to automatically terminate exploration as soon as validation loss stops improving when training with the new quarterly dataset.
razon_rescate: Los features exactos (warm start, TRANSFER_LEARNING, early stopping) no se ensenan; solo AMT como concepto. | La AIP evalua sub-features/parametros concretos (warm start type) y decision de optimizacion con presupuesto limitado; las cartas solo definen AMT.
feature_faltante: warm start; TRANSFER_LEARNING warm start type; early stopping

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A social media platform is developing an ML model to moderate user-generated content. The platform stores large volumes of textual and document data in Amazon S3. It uses Amazon Textract to extract text from uploaded PDFs or images, and Amazon SageMaker AI to train custom language models that classify comments based on sentiment, context, and topic relevance. The moderation team aims to enhance safety by detecting toxic or harmful language in real-time, including hate speech, harassment, and explicit threats. The solution must integrate seamlessly with the existing SageMaker AI inference pipeline, handle high throughput, and provide confidence scores for each classification, allowing content flagged as toxic to be reviewed or blocked automatically. Which of the solutions provides a managed solution for detecting toxicity in text to support this ML pipeline with safety classifiers?

options.text: Utilize Amazon Comprehend sentiment analysis to detect negative comments and block content automatically.
options.rationale: because sentiment analysis only identifies the overall tone of text as positive, negative, or neutral. It does not specifically detect abusive or toxic language, so relying on it would typically miss harmful content or misclassify non-toxic negative comments as toxic.

options.text: Use Amazon Translate to convert text into another language before moderation to reduce offensive content.
options.rationale: . Amazon Translation does not inherently detect toxicity. It simply converts text from one language to another, which would only change the language but not address abusive or harmful content. Moderation would remain ineffective if the goal is to identify toxic text.

options.text: Utilize Amazon Comprehend toxicity detection to identify abusive or harmful language in text.
Use Amazon Bedrock to fine-tune a foundation model for general language understanding.
options.rationale: . While Bedrock can be used to fine-tune foundation models, it does not automatically detect toxic language. Fine-tuning for general language understanding only provides broader NLP capabilities, and toxicity detection would require additional custom development, which is typically more complex and time-consuming than using a managed service like Comprehend.

correct_text: Utilize Amazon Comprehend toxicity detection to identify abusive or harmful language in text.
razon_rescate: El feature especifico (Comprehend toxicity detection) no se ensena; las cartas solo cubren Comprehend para sentimiento/entidades, distinto objetivo examinable.

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A global enterprise is building an internal generative AI environment that performs text insights and embedding generation by using Amazon Titan models running on Amazon Bedrock. Multiple engineering divisions intend to integrate these capabilities into various business applications. The organization manages all cloud accounts through AWS Organizations, with distinct organizational units (OUs) representing each department. Executive leadership requires an access framework that enforces the principle of least privilege and restricts interaction with selected foundation models (FMs). The access approach must follow strict role-based access control (RBAC) standards and must integrate seamlessly with the centralized identity provider (IdP) to maintain unified governance across the enterprise environment. Only department-approved development teams must be authorized to invoke specific models, and every model interaction must be recorded for auditing and compliance evaluations. Which action ensures the requirements are met in the most secure manner?

options.text: Enable Amazon Cognito user pools for authentication and map users to groups representing each department. Attach IAM policies to the groups to manage Bedrock model access. Configure Amazon CloudWatch Logs to capture Bedrock request activity for review.
options.rationale: because Amazon Cognito primarily provides authentication for application end users, not centralized workforce identities that span multiple AWS accounts. This prevents it from integrating with AWS Organizations or enforcing governance across organizational units. The IAM policies attached to Cognito groups cannot establish department-level RBAC or least-privilege controls in a multi-account environment, and CloudWatch Logs does not control or restrict access to foundation models. As a whole, the combination of services in this option cannot deliver OU-level governance, centralized identity integration, or tightly scoped access to specific Bedrock models.

options.text: Implement IAM identity policies with tag-based access controls for development teams. Assign resource tags to Bedrock models and allow model invocation only when the requester’s session tags match. Use AWS Config rules to track configuration changes across OUs.
options.rationale: because tag-based authorization simply cannot be applied to Amazon Bedrock foundation models. Bedrock models do not support resource tagging, which means no tag-based condition can restrict which teams invoke which models. Without taggable resources, session tags cannot enforce departmental boundaries, and AWS Config cannot compensate for this limitation because it only monitors configuration states rather than enforcing access control. As a result, this option is unable to provide controlled FM access or the governance required across multiple OUs.

options.text: Enable SAML federation to AWS IAM Identity Center from the corporate IdP. Build permissions sets for each OU to authorize only designated Bedrock model invocations. Attach an SCP to prevent model usage outside the approved set.

Implement IAM policies that reference Bedrock Guardrails and enforce model-restricted conditions. Build Amazon EventBridge rules that trigger warnings for unexpected behavior. Record Bedrock API calls through AWS CloudTrail for auditing.
options.rationale: because Bedrock Guardrails typically influence safety filters and content moderation rather than enforce which teams are allowed to invoke specific models. Guardrails do not provide access segmentation across departments, and EventBridge notifications only detect activity rather than block unauthorized access. Since IAM policies alone cannot enforce organization-wide RBAC for Bedrock within separate OUs, this option cannot meet the requirements for strict governance, least-privilege enforcement, or departmental model restrictions.

correct_text: Enable SAML federation to AWS IAM Identity Center from the corporate IdP. Build permissions sets for each OU to authorize only designated Bedrock model invocations. Attach an SCP to prevent model usage outside the approved set.
razon_rescate: El objetivo combina SAML/IAM Identity Center + permission sets + restriccion de modelos Bedrock, nada de lo cual se ensena; las cartas solo cubren SCP/Organizations genericos.

category: AIP – Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
stem: A multinational digital payments provider is designing a real-time fraud detection platform using Amazon SageMaker AI for training and hosting machine learning models, and Amazon Comprehend for analyzing unstructured transaction descriptions. The AI development team has consolidated years of historical transaction data from multiple regions into a single data lake. Each record in this dataset contains the following fields: client_identifier (string) account_category (integer) payment_value (float) account_duration (integer) operation_status (string) with possible values “legitimate” or “suspicious” Before deploying the model to production, the AI developer must prepare the data to ensure compatibility with SageMaker AI built-in algorithms and maintain a valid label structure for classification. Which preprocessing step should the AI developer perform before training the model in SageMaker AI?

options.text: Retain all fields and use Comprehend to transform operation_status into sentiment-based numeric scores before starting the training job.
options.rationale: because Amazon Comprehend is primarily designed for natural language processing tasks like sentiment analysis, entity recognition, and topic modeling on unstructured text. The operation_status field is already a structured categorical label (“legitimate” or “suspicious”) and does not require sentiment scoring. Using Comprehend here would be unnecessary and misaligned with the goal of preparing a classification label.

options.text: Exclude the client_identifier field and encode operation_status into numeric labels, then proceed with launching the model training phase in SageMaker AI.
Exclude both client_identifier and operation_status fields to reduce data correlation, and initiate model training using the remaining attributes.
options.rationale: because removing operation_status eliminates the target label needed for supervised classification. Without it, the model cannot learn to distinguish between legitimate and suspicious transactions.

options.text: Convert all fields into string format to maintain data consistency, and then start the model training phase in SageMaker AI.
options.rationale: because SageMaker AI built-in algorithms typically expect numerical input features for training. Converting all fields to strings would degrade model performance and prevent proper feature engineering, especially for fields like payment_value and account_duration which are inherently numeric.

correct_text: Exclude the client_identifier field and encode operation_status into numeric labels, then proceed with launching the model training phase in SageMaker AI.
razon_rescate: Ninguna carta ensena la preparacion de etiquetas/exclusion de features para compatibilidad con algoritmos built-in; solape solo de escenario fraude.

category: AIP – Testing, Validation, and Troubleshooting
stem: A generative AI developer manages a production generative model endpoint in Amazon SageMaker AI, with Model Monitor and Amazon SageMaker Clarify enabled. The developer recently deployed a newly retrained model to replace an older version, and Model Monitor has been configured to track data quality and distribution drift. SageMaker Clarify continues to provide explainability and bias metrics for the same endpoint. The team also monitors for response drift to detect any unexpected shifts in model output patterns following the retraining. Despite the model being updated and serving new inference traffic based on a more current dataset, the monitoring job continues to show violations. The developer has confirmed that the new dataset is statistically representative of the current traffic, but the violations still persist. Which corrective action should the developer take to resolve the persistent violations in Model Monitor?

options.text: Trigger a new SageMaker model training job with the existing baseline dataset to refresh the model's performance.
options.rationale: because retraining the model with the same baseline dataset will not resolve the issue. The problem lies with the outdated baseline, and simply retraining the model will not fix the mismatch between the baseline and the new data distribution. The baseline needs to be regenerated to reflect the updated traffic.

options.text: Adjust the SageMaker Model Monitor threshold settings to reduce the frequency of violations.
options.rationale: because this action does not address the root cause of the problem, which is an outdated baseline. Adjusting the threshold settings may reduce the number of alerts, but it will not correct the underlying comparison issue between the monitoring data and the baseline dataset, which is causing the persistent violations. This will affect only the frequency of alerts, not the actual problem.

options.text: Remove the current model endpoint and recreate it with the same configuration as the original one.
options.rationale: because this step will not update the SageMaker Model Monitor baseline. Rebuilding the model endpoint does not primarily change the baseline data used for monitoring. Recreating the endpoint will not affect the monitoring configuration, meaning the model will continue to be compared against the outdated baseline, causing the violations to persist.

options.text: Perform a baseline job on the new training data and configure Model Monitor to reference the new baseline statistics.

correct_text: Perform a baseline job on the new training data and configure Model Monitor to reference the new baseline statistics.
razon_rescate: El objetivo examinable es la accion correctiva de re-baseline (resolver violaciones persistentes), no la deteccion; ninguna carta ensena re-baselining.

category: AIP – Implementation and Integration
stem: A global broadcasting enterprise, TD Studios, operates an intelligent content-management platform built on Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The platform uses SageMaker to coordinate large-scale data preparation and model-training workflows, enabling automated feature extraction and experimentation across thousands of multimedia assets. At the same time, Bedrock AgentCore serves as the orchestration layer that connects multiple AWS AI services, allowing agents to invoke specialized models and enrich content with generative summaries and metadata for semantic search. The enterprise recently expanded its media repository with several petabytes of newly acquired, unlabeled images, videos, podcasts, and written transcripts stored in Amazon S3. The Research and Curation division, composed primarily of content analysts with limited machine learning expertise, must now enable automatic tagging and indexing of this data to support entity-based search and cross-referencing. The enterprise wants to extend its existing Bedrock AgentCore workflow to handle this new data without performing any model training, manual labeling, or infrastructure provisioning. The solution must deliver accurate tagging across multiple modalities and achieve rapid implementation suitable for a non-specialized research team. Which solution provides the fastest and most effective approach to automatically index and categorize the multimedia assets?

options.text: Use AWS Batch to periodically run containerized Python scripts that perform speech-to-text conversion, image feature extraction, and topic modeling across the media files.
options.rationale: because AWS Batch is primarily designed for running batch computing jobs at scale, not for managed AI or ML tasks. While it can execute custom scripts that call ML models, it does not provide built-in capabilities for multimedia analysis or metadata extraction. This approach would add unnecessary complexity since it requires manual configuration, job orchestration, and maintenance compared to using fully managed AI services like Amazon Rekognition, Amazon Comprehend, and Amazon Transcribe.

options.text: Configure Amazon Polly, Amazon Translate, and Amazon Lex within a SageMaker pipeline to convert audio and text into multilingual transcripts and conversational responses for cataloging media.
options.rationale: because these services are only intended for speech synthesis, translation, and conversational interfaces, not for tagging or classifying media assets. Amazon Polly converts text to natural-sounding speech, Amazon Translate handles language translation, and Amazon Lex builds chatbots. None of these features support visual detection or entity extraction, which are necessary to index and categorize multimedia content automatically.

options.text: Convert audio to text using Amazon Transcribe, then use SageMaker’s Neural Topic Model (NTM) and Object Detection to assign category tags across the dataset.
options.rationale: because SageMaker’s built-in NTM and Object Detection are training algorithms that primarily require configuring and running training jobs, and Object Detection needs labeled datasets with annotations. This workflow introduces model training, tuning, and data labeling, which is slower and more complex than using managed AI services for direct multimedia tagging.

options.text: Leverage Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Transcribe, and Amazon Rekognition to categorize and tag multimedia content automatically

correct_text: Leverage Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Transcribe, and Amazon Rekognition to categorize and tag multimedia content automatically
razon_rescate: Ninguna carta ensena la combinacion de servicios de IA multimodal para tagging; las cartas tratan CDN/replicacion/contact center. | La AIP pide una decision de diseno multimodal especifica; las cartas tratan temas no relacionados (CloudFront/DynamoDB) aunque Bloom alto, el contenido tecnico no coinc
feature_faltante: Combinacion de servicios AI multimodal; agentcore

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: A global insurance technology company built a claims automation system using Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint and Amazon Rekognition. Rekognition analyzes uploaded vehicle images to detect the severity and type of damage, while SageMaker uses this information, along with other structured features such as vehicle age, mileage, and estimated repair cost, to predict claim approval probability and estimated settlement time. During initial training, the model assigned greater weight to the damage severity score and repair cost estimate as the most influential features for decision-making. However, recent observations suggest that the deployed model on the SageMaker AI endpoint might now be emphasizing vehicle age more heavily than damage severity, resulting in inconsistent predictions and potential policy compliance issues. The data science team must implement a monitoring solution that detects when the feature weight or attribution importance of input variables shifts in production and automatically triggers alerts for investigation. Which of the following should be implemented?

options.text: Deploy SageMaker Clarify to perform bias and explainability analysis on the training dataset. Use Amazon CloudWatch to alert if Clarify reports significant changes in feature attribution or fairness metrics.
options.rationale: because SageMaker Clarify is primarily designed for static analysis. It helps detect bias and explainability issues during model development and training, not in real-time production. It doesn’t continuously monitor deployed models or track live changes in feature attribution, so it won’t detect if the model starts prioritizing vehicle age over damage severity during inference.

options.text: Enable SageMaker DataCapture to log inference inputs and outputs. Build a custom pipeline to analyze feature distributions and model responses over time. Use Amazon CloudWatch to alert when significant shifts in input patterns or predictions are detected.
options.rationale: because while DataCapture is typically useful for logging inference data, it doesn’t natively track feature attribution. You’d need to build a custom pipeline to extract and analyze SHAP values or other attribution metrics, which adds complexity and overhead. It’s a less direct and less efficient solution compared to using ModelExplainabilityMonitor, which is purpose-built for this task.

options.text: Use ModelExplainabilityMonitor class with a SHAP-based baseline to detect feature attribution drift in production. Regularly compare how the model assigns importance to input features against the baseline, and configure Amazon CloudWatch to alert stakeholders when attribution values drift beyond acceptable thresholds.

Implement a baseline for model quality using the ModelQualityMonitor class. The baseline will evaluate key performance metrics such as accuracy and recall, with periodic checks to identify any significant shifts in model performance. Set up an Amazon CloudWatch if the model’s quality metrics diverge from the baseline.
options.rationale: because ModelQualityMonitor focuses on performance metrics like accuracy, precision, and recall, not on how the model weighs input features. It won’t detect attribution drift unless the change in feature importance leads to a measurable drop in performance, which may not always happen. This makes it insufficient for detecting subtle but impactful shifts in decision logic.

correct_text: Use ModelExplainabilityMonitor class with a SHAP-based baseline to detect feature attribution drift in production. Regularly compare how the model assigns importance to input features against the baseline, and configure Amazon CloudWatch to alert stakeholders when attribution values drift beyond acceptable thresholds.
razon_rescate: El feature exacto (ModelExplainabilityMonitor + baseline SHAP) no se ensena; feature attribution drift solo aparece como distractor. | La AIP evalua una clase/feature especifica y su config de umbrales; las cartas solo definen deteccion de drift genericamente. Bloom AIP=alto vs carta=medio.

category: AIP – AI Safety, Security, and Governance
stem: A financial services company needs to build a predictive model to identify fraudulent transactions using historical customer data, which includes sensitive information such as credit card numbers. The company plans to use Amazon SageMaker AI to train the model and Amazon Comprehend to extract features from the text-based data in the dataset. The company must ensure that all customer data is securely encrypted and that any personally identifiable information (PII), including credit card numbers, is redacted before the data is used for model training. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.text: Use SageMaker AI Data Wrangler to process the customer data and apply encryption using a custom algorithm. Use AWS CLI to automate the upload of the encrypted data to Amazon S3, then train the model using the encrypted dataset.
options.rationale: because SageMaker AI Data Wrangler is a data preparation tool and is not designed for PII redaction or encryption. Applying a custom encryption algorithm does not meet compliance standards for securing sensitive financial data — AWS KMS is the recommended approach for managed encryption. Additionally, while AWS CLI can automate S3 uploads, it plays no role in addressing the core requirements of PII redaction or secure encryption.

options.text: Use Comprehend to detect and redact PII from the customer data, then store the redacted data in Amazon S3 and train the model using SageMaker AI. Encrypt the customer data using a custom algorithm.
options.rationale: because although Amazon Comprehend is typically suitable for PII detection and redaction, the use of a custom encryption algorithm introduces risk. Custom encryption may not be compliant with industry standards and could complicate integration with AWS services. AWS KMS is the preferred method for encryption in secure ML workflows.

options.text: Use SageMaker AI Principal Component Analysis (PCA) algorithm to reduce the dimensionality of the customer data before training the model. Ensure that sensitive information, like credit card numbers, is removed during the PCA process and the data is stored in Amazon S3.
options.rationale: because PCA is primarily a dimensionality reduction technique, not a data sanitization or redaction tool. It does not guarantee the removal of PII such as credit card numbers. Relying on PCA for PII removal is not secure or compliant with data protection standards.

options.text: Encrypt customer data with AWS KMS in Amazon S3 before importing it into SageMaker AI. Use AWS Glue to redact credit card numbers from the customer data before using it for model training.

correct_text: Encrypt customer data with AWS KMS in Amazon S3 before importing it into SageMaker AI. Use AWS Glue to redact credit card numbers from the customer data before using it for model training.
razon_rescate: Ninguna carta ensena Glue para redaccion de PII ni el combo KMS+Glue; Macie (descubrimiento) es servicio distinto al objetivo.

category: AIP – Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
stem: A data science team is developing a computer vision model using Amazon SageMaker AI to classify product images that customers upload. In addition to image features, the team plans to integrate Amazon Comprehend to analyze customer feedback text associated with each image. During data preparation, the team noticed that one of the numerical features representing image brightness seemed to affect the model’s convergence rate during training. The lead ML engineer wants to explore how the brightness values are distributed in the dataset before deciding to apply normalization. The engineer uses SageMaker Data Wrangler for feature engineering and data preprocessing. Which actions should the engineer take to best understand the range and distribution of the brightness feature values before transformation?

options.text: The engineer should use Comprehend to perform sentiment analysis on the brightness values to determine if normalization is needed.
options.rationale: . Amazon Comprehend is primarily designed for natural language processing (NLP) tasks, not numerical data analysis. It can extract sentiment, key phrases, or entities from text, but it cannot visualize or interpret numerical values like image brightness. Using Comprehend here would be inappropriate because it deals only with text-based insights and provides no tools for distribution analysis or feature normalization decisions. The brightness feature, being numerical, must be examined visually through tools like SageMaker Data Wrangler, not through text analysis.

options.text: The engineer should export the dataset to Amazon S3 and use AWS Glue DataBrew to create a box plot visualization of the brightness feature.
options.rationale: . Although AWS Glue DataBrew can visualize and transform data, exporting to it in this case would simply add unnecessary complexity to the workflow. Since the data is already being processed within Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler, moving it to another service for basic visualization would be inefficient. Furthermore, a box plot provides a summary of data spread and outliers but does not reveal the full frequency distribution of the brightness values as clearly as a histogram does.

options.text: The engineer should use the SageMaker Data Wrangler histogram visualization to inspect the range of values for the brightness feature and identify any outliers.
The engineer should use SageMaker Clarify to detect data bias in the brightness feature before performing any normalization.
options.rationale: . Amazon SageMaker Clarify is typically used for bias detection and explainability in machine learning models, not for basic exploratory data analysis. Clarify helps identify potential fairness issues or bias in datasets and models but does not provide the kind of distribution-focused visualization needed to evaluate the range of a numerical feature. Using Clarify here would only assess data bias, not the actual spread or variance of the brightness values. Therefore, it does not fulfill the requirement of inspecting the feature’s distribution before normalization.

correct_text: The engineer should use the SageMaker Data Wrangler histogram visualization to inspect the range of values for the brightness feature and identify any outliers.
razon_rescate: Ninguna carta ensena Data Wrangler ni su visualizacion de histograma; solape solo tematico (SageMaker/vision).

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: A digital media company operates a web platform where customers upload high-resolution product and marketing images that require automated text generation for accessibility and search optimization. Each uploaded image can reach up to 60 MB in size, and the platform experiences unpredictable spikes in traffic during global promotional campaigns. All uploaded images are securely stored in an Amazon S3 bucket, which acts as the central repository for incoming media files. The company uses Amazon Rekognition to analyze images, detecting objects, scenes, and other visual features that form the foundation of metadata. The extracted information is passed to Amazon Bedrock, which uses a foundation model to generate detailed natural language captions describing the image content accurately and contextually. The ML workflow automatically starts processing when new images are uploaded to the S3 bucket. The GenAI developer must design a solution that scales automatically to handle fluctuating workloads, maintains high availability during traffic spikes, and operates with minimal infrastructure management overhead. Which solution fulfills these requirements with minimal infrastructure management and operational effort?

options.text: Build a containerized processing pipeline using Amazon ECS on Fargate that runs on a schedule to handle uploaded images and insert processed data into Amazon Aurora.
options.rationale: because ECS scheduled tasks are primarily designed for running periodic jobs based on a fixed schedule rather than responding to event-driven triggers such as new S3 uploads. While ECS Fargate removes the need to manage servers, it still requires manual configuration for scheduling, monitoring, and scaling. This setup would not provide the dynamic responsiveness and automated scaling required to handle unpredictable spikes in image upload volume.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon SageMaker Asynchronous Inference endpoint with a scaling policy that automatically adjusts capacity and processes inference requests for each image in the S3 bucket.
Launch an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to host an inference application that monitors the primary S3 bucket for new image uploads and stores processed results in a separate S3 bucket.
options.rationale: because EC2-based solutions typically require ongoing infrastructure management, including instance patching, scaling configurations, and monitoring. Even though Auto Scaling provides elasticity, this approach adds operational complexity and lacks the built-in queuing and asynchronous processing capabilities of managed inference services. The result is higher administrative overhead and less efficient scaling compared to a fully managed solution like SageMaker Asynchronous Inference.

options.text: Use Amazon SQS to queue image-processing tasks and trigger AWS Lambda functions that run Rekognition and Bedrock processing for each uploaded image.
options.rationale: because Lambda is just not designed for large, resource-intensive ML workflows. Lambda has strict limits on payload size, memory, and execution time, making it unsuitable for handling high-resolution images up to 60 MB or for running long-running inference jobs. During traffic spikes, Lambda would struggle to scale efficiently for this type of workload, leading to failures or timeouts. The company needs a solution specifically designed for scalable asynchronous ML inference, which Lambda cannot provide.

correct_text: Deploy an Amazon SageMaker Asynchronous Inference endpoint with a scaling policy that automatically adjusts capacity and processes inference requests for each image in the S3 bucket.
razon_rescate: Las cartas tratan Storage Gateway/Rekognition para media on-premises, no ensenan Asynchronous Inference; solape solo de tema imagenes. | La AIP evalua eleccion de tipo de inferencia para payload grande/picos; las cartas tratan Storage Gateway/Rekognition, no el nivel de diseno de inferencia async.

category: AIP – Implementation and Integration
stem: A data science team is running an anti-financial crime workload using Amazon SageMaker Training and SageMaker Feature Store. The team stores transactional features inside the Feature Store offline store, and those features are periodically retrieved and consumed by SageMaker model training jobs inside a scheduled retraining pipeline. The binary classifier is used for real-time fraud detection involving regulated payment flows, but the team is consistently observing a very high count of false negatives, even though the overall model accuracy is greater than 96%. The core issue is the severe class imbalance condition, where fraud transactions represent less than one-half of one percent of the entire dataset, and historical fraud samples remain extremely limited. The goal is to increase the model’s ability to correctly detect fraudulent cases. The team wants to directly correct this imbalance problem before running the next retraining cycle. Which solution will increase the fraudulent case detection performance?

options.text: Perform random oversampling on the non-fraudulent transactions to equalize batch sizes during training.
options.rationale: because it increases the number of majority class samples (non-fraud), which worsens the class imbalance. This leads to further bias toward the non-fraud class and reduces the model’s ability to detect fraud.

options.text: Enable early stopping in SageMaker to automatically halt training when the model's accuracy on the validation set no longer improves.
options.rationale: because early stopping only prevents overfitting but does not address class imbalance or improve the model’s ability to detect rare fraudulent cases. It’s a general optimization technique, not a targeted solution for this scenario.

options.text: Enable automatic model tuning in SageMaker using Bayesian Optimization to find the best hyperparameters by running multiple training jobs. Increase the number of hyperparameter tuning jobs to explore a broader range of hyperparameter values and potentially improve model performance.
options.rationale: because while hyperparameter tuning primarily enhances overall model performance, it does not solve the underlying issue of class imbalance. Without addressing the skewed distribution, tuning alone won’t significantly reduce false negatives.

options.text: Integrate a preprocessing step that applies the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) on the minority fraudulent transaction class only before the training run begins.

correct_text: Integrate a preprocessing step that applies the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) on the minority fraudulent transaction class only before the training run begins.
razon_rescate: La tecnica exacta (SMOTE / oversampling sintetico de clase minoritaria) no se ensena; una carta solo menciona 'oversampling aleatorio' como contexto, no SMOTE. | La AIP pide una tecnica de correccion especifica (SMOTE); las cartas solo definen deteccion/monitoreo del desbalance, no la tecnica de rem

category: AIP – Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
stem: A team of AI engineers is developing a churn prediction model using Amazon SageMaker AI. The team imports customer interaction and billing data into SageMaker Data Wrangler for data preparation and feature engineering. During exploratory data analysis, the team discovered that only about 8% of customers in the dataset have churned, causing a significant class imbalance. The team plans to launch a SageMaker training job using an XGBoost model to predict churn. However, initial training results show that the model consistently predicts the majority “non-churn” class, leading to poor recall for churned customers. The data scientist must address the imbalance to improve model performance and ensure the training dataset adequately represents both classes. Which approach should the team take to resolve this issue before starting the SageMaker training job?

options.text: Enable SageMaker Model Monitor to detect data drift and class imbalance after deployment, and use its reports to adjust the model’s prediction thresholds manually.
options.rationale: . Model Monitor is primarily designed to continuously observe deployed models in production for data drift, feature quality, and bias changes over time. It does not modify or rebalance the training dataset or retrain models automatically. Using Model Monitor here would only identify issues after the model is deployed, rather than correcting the imbalance before training. Therefore, while it is a valuable post-deployment tool, it does not address the root cause of poor recall due to dataset imbalance.

options.text: Apply a Random Undersampling in SageMaker Data Wrangler to remove samples from the majority non-churn class before training the model.
options.rationale: . Although this can balance the dataset, it typically leads to the loss of important information from the majority class, reducing the overall dataset size and potentially weakening model generalization. Removing too many samples may degrade model accuracy in churn prediction problems, where data from retained customers provides valuable context.
