options.text: Use SageMaker Clarify to analyze the class imbalance and generate bias metrics. Document the imbalance findings before retraining the model.
options.rationale: . Clarify is primarily used to provide insights into model bias, explainability, and fairness across features before and after training. While documenting imbalance findings is a good practice, it does not actively solve the imbalance problem that causes poor model recall. Therefore, Clarify serves a diagnostic purpose, not a corrective one, in this scenario.

options.text: Perform the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) in SageMaker Data Wrangler to rebalance the churn dataset before running the SageMaker training job.

correct_text: Perform the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) in SageMaker Data Wrangler to rebalance the churn dataset before running the SageMaker training job.
razon_rescate: El feature exacto (SMOTE en Data Wrangler) no se ensena; solape solo tematico (desbalance de clases). | La AIP evalua la tecnica especifica (SMOTE) y el feature de Data Wrangler; las cartas no ensenan SMOTE ni el paso en Data Wrangler.

category: AIP – Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
stem: A global market research firm stores thousands of recorded analyst briefings in Amazon S3. The data science division uses Amazon SageMaker AI JumpStart to experiment with pretrained NLP models for text classification and Amazon Polly to synthesize sample voice outputs for model validation. Before processing, the team uses AWS Glue Data Quality to validate and standardize incoming audio metadata and transcript outputs to ensure consistency across all recordings. The next project phase requires grouping all recorded discussions by the conversation themes, such as equity strategy, macroeconomic policy, and currency trends. The AI developer must choose an approach that automatically categorizes these recordings by topic, while minimizing custom development effort. Which solution will meet this requirement most efficiently?

options.text: Run Amazon Transcribe jobs followed by an Amazon Comprehend custom classifier to assign predefined topic labels to each transcript.
options.rationale: because it typically requires building and training a custom classifier in Comprehend, which involves manual data labeling, model training, and evaluation. This adds complexity and development effort, contrary to the goal of minimizing custom work.

options.text: Build a custom data labeling workflow in SageMaker AI Ground Truth, then execute Amazon Transcribe jobs to convert audio to text and use SageMaker AI semantic segmentation to group the labeled outputs.
options.rationale: because semantic segmentation is primarily designed for image data, not text or audio. This approach misapplies the algorithm and introduces unnecessary manual labeling and orchestration steps.

options.text: Generate transcripts through Amazon Transcribe jobs, then sequentially train both the SageMaker AI semantic segmentation algorithm and Neural Topic Model (NTM) algorithm to manually group textual content into themes.
options.rationale: because it involves manual training of multiple models, including one (semantic segmentation) that’s irrelevant to text data. This increases development effort and complexity unnecessarily

options.text: Configure Amazon Transcribe jobs to process all recordings into text, followed by an Amazon Comprehend topic detection job that identifies and clusters conversation topics.

correct_text: Configure Amazon Transcribe jobs to process all recordings into text, followed by an Amazon Comprehend topic detection job that identifies and clusters conversation topics.
razon_rescate: El feature exacto (Comprehend topic detection / topic modeling para clustering) no se ensena; la carta de audio usa Transcribe+Comprehend para KEY PHRASES, objetivo distinto al topic detection.

category: AIP – Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications
stem: A global e-commerce platform utilizes Amazon SageMaker AI to implement a real-time recommendation system that provides personalized product suggestions. The model is developed using SageMaker Studio. Once trained, the model is hosted on a SageMaker endpoint, enabling it to deliver inferences in real time. Additionally, the company employs Amazon Comprehend to analyze customer feedback and sentiment derived from reviews and product ratings. This analysis helps the company better understand customer preferences and enhance its recommendations. As the business prepares for major sales events, the operations team observes that increased customer activity results in significant delays when retrieving product recommendations, ultimately leading to a poor user experience. To address this issue, there is a need to adjust the target tracking scaling policy on the SageMaker endpoint. The goal is to ensure effective scaling during high-traffic periods, preventing latency from adversely affecting the customer experience. Which solution will best optimize the scaling of the SageMaker inference endpoint?

options.text: Configure a scheduled scaling policy to increase the capacity of the SageMaker inference endpoint before the sales events begin.
Use AWS Lambda to periodically restart the SageMaker endpoint during peak traffic to refresh instance performance.
options.rationale: because restarting the endpoint does not improve scalability or performance. It introduces unnecessary downtime and does not address the root cause of latency, which is insufficient capacity during peak load.

options.text: Implement a step scaling policy for the SageMaker inference endpoint that scales based on resource utilization metrics such as CPU and memory usage.
options.rationale: because SageMaker endpoints do not expose granular CPU or memory metrics for scaling. Instead, scaling should be typically based on metrics like invocations per instance, which are more relevant to inference workloads.

options.text: Increase the instance size of the SageMaker endpoint to a larger instance type to accommodate higher traffic during sales events.
options.rationale: because while it may temporarily improve performance, it’s a static solution that lacks flexibility. It doesn’t dynamically adjust to changing traffic patterns and may only lead to overprovisioning or underutilization outside peak periods.

correct_text: Configure a scheduled scaling policy to increase the capacity of the SageMaker inference endpoint before the sales events begin.
razon_rescate: El feature exacto (scheduled scaling policy) no se ensena; las cartas cubren auto-scaling/target-tracking en general pero no el escalado programado. | La AIP distingue una sub-feature de escalado (scheduled scaling) para un patron de trafico predecible; las cartas solo definen auto-scaling generico.
